dedupe_keys.name: natural solutions tool greater chicago watershed scale parcel prioritisation map for green infrastructure

description: The Natural Solutions Tool is a web map that ranks parcels across Chicago-area watersheds by how well they suit green infrastructure and other nature-based solutions, so that funders and planners can steer investment to communities of greatest need. It is a project of the Greater Chicago Watershed Alliance, created and managed by the planning team of Friends of the Chicago River with the Trust for Public Land and local experts, and its 2025 update extended coverage north to the Wisconsin border across all of Lake County. Coverage is the Chicago region's watersheds; every parcel is tagged with the results of the analysis layers, built from county parcel data, park boundaries, watershed and administrative boundaries, zoning and the Calumet green infrastructure baseline inventory. Format and access: an interactive mapping portal, downloadable PDF maps, a data description sheet and a demo video, all free to use. Licence: not stated on the overview page; free. Caveats: it prioritises sites, not simulating performance, and depends on data as of 2023 to 2025. It supports climate adaptation and capacity planning for stormwater green infrastructure. Related catalogue records are ParkServe and Regrid parcel data, which feed it.
